summary: Venkatesh constructs a graded extension of the Hecke algebra — the derived Hecke algebra, the Ext-algebra Ext^*_{S[G_v]}(S[G_v/K_v], S[G_v/K_v]) of the smooth induction — which acts on the cohomology of an arithmetic manifold Y(K) with the Ext-degree raising cohomological degree. The higher Ext-groups are almost annihilated by q_v − 1, so the theory is used at primes with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^n; at such primes he proves a derived Satake isomorphism identifying the local algebra with the Weyl invariants of the corresponding torus algebra, hence graded commutative. Globally he asks whether the cohomology is generated over this algebra by its minimal degree, and proves it in two cases: for the Hecke-trivial part, where the algebra acts rationally by cup product (Theorem 5.2, via Quillen's computation of the cohomology of finite groups of Lie type and a Chebotarev argument), and under Taylor–Wiles hypotheses (Theorem 7.6, via patched complexes). The main result, the reciprocity law of Theorem 8.5, produces an action of the dual of the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H^1_f(Z[1/Σ], Ad^*ρ(1)) — a free Z_p-module of rank δ — by degree-one endomorphisms, characterised by agreeing with derived Hecke operators at all Taylor–Wiles primes, so that the derived Hecke algebra contains, and under a mild hypothesis equals, the exterior algebra on that Selmer group. Conjecture 8.8 then asserts that the motivic Q-lattice inside the Selmer group — Scholl's integral motivic cohomology H^1_mot((M_coad)_Z, Q(1)) of the coadjoint motive — preserves rational cohomology: a hidden action of motivic cohomology on H^*(Y(K), Q), computable p-adically by derived Hecke operators. The atlas plans the setting but not the object: ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces builds symmetric spaces, local systems, chain complexes and Hecke correspondences; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups builds smooth representations, Hecke algebras over rings and the classical Satake; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra builds the patching of complexes with cohomology in several degrees; and the motivic side is planned in MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles and PeriodsAndSpecialValues. Searches return no hit anywhere for 'derived Hecke' or 'derived deformation'.

items.name: Arithmetic manifolds
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a number field F (in the introduction a semisimple Q-group) and K = prod_v K_v an open compact subgroup of G(A_{F,f}) with K_v hyperspecial for all but finitely many v. Then Y(K) = G(F)\(S_inf x G(A_f))/K (17), where S_inf is the quotient of G(F (x) R) by a maximal compact connected subgroup; it is a finite union of locally symmetric spaces Gamma\S_inf, and its cohomology is taken in the orbifold sense. Put delta = rank G(F (x) R) - rank(maximal compact subgroup) (18) and define q by 2q + delta = dim Y(K). A place v is good for K when K_v is hyperspecial and G is quasisplit at v; the level of K is the finite set of places that are not good.
items.locator: Section 1, p. 2; Section 1.2, equations (3)-(4), p. 5; Section 1.7 (Notation), equations (17)-(19), p. 14; Section 2.6, p. 19 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: ALS.0 constructs symmetric spaces with their arithmetic components and ALS.1 the local systems and chain complexes on them; the invariants δ and q are the standard ones of Borel–Wallach. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Substantively right, but the printed setting (Section 1.7, (17)-(19)) is more general and fixes conventions the item omits: G reductive over a number field F (semisimple over Q only in the introduction), K = prod_v K_v with K_v hyperspecial for almost all v, Y(K) taken as an orbifold, and the notion of good place and level. The notation section is 1.7 in print and 1.8 in v3 (the v3 Section 1.7 was the acknowledgements, moved to the end in print).

items.name: The shape of the tempered cohomology
items.statement: For a tempered cuspidal character χ of the Hecke algebra one has dim H^{q+i}(Y(K), Q)_χ = C(δ, i) · dim H^q(Y(K), Q)_χ, so the same Hecke eigensystem occurs in the δ + 1 consecutive degrees q, …, q + δ.
items.locator: Section 1.2, equation (5), p. 5 (citing Borel-Wallach, Theorem III.5.1, and Borel, Corollary 5.5) (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The numerical phenomenon the whole paper explains. It is a statement about (g, K)-cohomology of tempered representations; the atlas plans locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology in ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces but not this computation. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Statement matches print. Locator: there is no equation (1.2.3) in either version; the paper numbers equations consecutively and this is (5). 'Tempered cuspidal' means: there are cuspidal automorphic pi_1, ..., pi_r, tempered at infinity, whose associated cohomology is exactly the generalised chi-eigenspace H^*(Y(K), C)_chi.

items.name: The usual Hecke algebra and its action
items.statement: For a good place v the spherical Hecke algebra is Hom_{S[G_v]}(S[G_v/K_v], S[G_v/K_v]); T denotes the subalgebra of End H^*(Y(K), Z_p) generated by all Hecke operators at good places, acting through Hecke correspondences.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 2; Section 2.2, p. 16 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: SR.1 constructs Hecke algebras over rings with their convolution and idempotents, and ALS.3 the Hecke correspondences on chain complexes of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces.

items.name: The local derived Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let G = G_v be the points of a reductive group over the nonarchimedean completion F_v, with residue field of characteristic p_v and size q_v, let U be an open compact subgroup of G and S a finite ring in which q_v is invertible. In the abelian category of smooth S[G]-modules (which has enough projectives), the derived Hecke algebra is the graded algebra H(G,U)_S := Ext^*(S[G/U], S[G/U]) with the Yoneda product; H^j(G,U) is the Ext^j summand, and with a fixed level structure H_{v,S} := H(G_v, K_v)_S. It is the cohomology of the dga Hom_{SG}(P,P) for any projective resolution P of S[G/U]; one may take P to be the compact induction from U to G of a free resolution Q of S over S[U/V], V a pro-p_v normal open subgroup of U (20).
items.locator: Section 1.1, equation (1), p. 2; Definition 2.2, equation (21), Section 2.2, p. 16 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The central new object. Schneider considered the same construction when S has characteristic v; here v is invertible on S, the opposite case. SR.0:derived-extension plans the derived extension of the smooth category and SR.1 the ordinary Hecke algebras, so the definition belongs in that direction. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Omits the standing hypotheses of Section 2.2 and 2.1: S is a finite ring in which q_v is invertible, and 'G-module' means a smooth S[G]-module (every vector has open stabiliser); this category is abelian with enough projectives (Section A.2). Locator: equation (1), not (1.1.1).

items.name: The higher Ext groups are almost killed by q_v − 1
items.statement: (Heuristic, Sections 1.1 and 2.4.) For G split and U hyperspecial, H(G,U) is isomorphic as an S-module to the sum over lambda in X_*(A)^+ of H^*(M_lambda(F_v), S), where M_lambda is the centraliser of lambda and F_v the residue field. For generic lambda, M_lambda is a split torus, so |M_lambda(F_v)| is a power of q_v - 1; hence if q_v - 1 is invertible in S the positive-degree parts of those summands vanish. The algebra is largest when q_v = 1 in S, which is why the theory is used at primes with q_v = 1 mod l^n.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 2; made precise in Section 2.4, p. 18 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The observation that selects the 'nice primes' at which the whole theory operates. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Informal as printed ('for elementary reasons'). The supporting computation is the size discussion of Section 2.4, which is only motivational (and contains a slip, see issues).

items.name: The global derived Hecke algebra and the strict one
items.statement: For each n, T-tilde_n is the subalgebra of End H^*(Y(K), Z/l^n) generated by the local derived Hecke algebras H_{v,Z/l^n} at all good places v of K not above l. The global derived Hecke algebra T-tilde (33) is the set of endomorphisms of H^*(Y(K), Z_l) = lim H^*(Y(K), Z/l^n) of the form lim t_n for compatible systems t_n in T-tilde_n (diagram (34)); its degree-zero part is the usual Hecke algebra T (Section 1.1). For V: places -> {0,1,...,inf}, T-tilde(V) is built the same way using H_{v,Z/l^n} only for n <= V(v). With V_0(v) = 0 for v not good and V_0(v) = v_l(q_v - 1) otherwise, T-tilde(V_0) is graded commutative by Section 3 when l does not divide |W|, and the strict global derived Hecke algebra is T' := the algebra generated by T-tilde(V_0) and all underived Hecke operators at good places prime to l. Then T is contained in T', which is contained in T-tilde.
items.locator: Section 1.1, pp. 2-3; Section 2.13, equation (33), pp. 25-26; Section 2.14, equation (36), pp. 26-27 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The paper does not know that 𝓗 is graded commutative in general; this is the reason for the strict variant, and one of the corrections made in the published version. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The strict algebra is not obtained by restricting to places at which the local algebras are graded commutative. Section 2.14 defines restricted algebras T(V) by using H_{v,Z/l^n} only for n <= V(v), takes V_0(v) = 0 at bad v and the l-adic valuation of q_v - 1 otherwise (the print says 'largest power', see issues), and sets the strict algebra T' := the algebra generated by T(V_0) and all underived Hecke operators at good places prime to l; so T is contained in T' contained in T-tilde. The note's claim that the strict variant is one of the corrections made in the published version is unsupported: Section 2.14 is the same in v3 and in print. In Sections 2.13-2.14 the coefficient prime is l.

items.name: The graded action on cohomology
items.statement: ℋ_{v,S} acts on H^*(Y(K), S) in a graded fashion: the Ext^i-component shifts cohomological degree by +i.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 2; Section 2.5, equation (26), p. 19; Section 2.6, pp. 19-20, with the Remark on p. 20 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The action is what makes the algebra relevant to the multiple-degree phenomenon; it is constructed abstractly in Section 2.6 and explicitly in Lemma 2.10. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Correct. The printed action is a right action written on the left (Remark, p. 20).

items.name: The generation question
items.statement: For a character χ : T → F_p of the usual Hecke algebra, one asks whether the map 𝓗 ⊗ H^{q}(Y(K), Z_p)_χ → H^*(Y(K), Z_p)_χ is surjective, i.e. whether the cohomology is generated over the derived Hecke algebra by its minimal degree q.
items.locator: Section 1.1, equation (2), p. 3 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: This is proved in two cases: Theorem 5.2 (the trivial representation) and Theorem 7.6 (under Taylor–Wiles hypotheses). Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): A question, not a theorem. Locator: equation (2), not (1.1.2). The text notes that T-tilde need not preserve the chi-part a priori and may be replaced by the strict algebra of Section 2.14.

items.name: Galois representations attached to cohomological characters
items.statement: To a tempered cuspidal χ there is conjecturally attached, for each p, a Galois representation ρ_χ : Gal(Q̄/Q) → ^LG(Q_p), crystalline at p for good p; this is known in several cases (Scholze).
items.locator: Section 1.2.1, p. 5 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The construction of Galois representations attached to the cohomology of locally symmetric spaces, including the torsion case, is planned in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Print: rho_chi takes values in the L-group with Q_p-bar coefficients, assumed for simplicity to be defined over Q_p; in general the L-group must be replaced by a slightly different group (Buzzard-Gee, Section 3.4); it should be crystalline at p for p not dividing the level. Review note on status: Looks unplanned at the cited stage: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.3 builds definite-unitary finite-slope eigenvarieties and interpolates Galois determinants; it does not attach Galois representations to (torsion) cohomology of general locally symmetric spaces. Scholze's construction cited here is the business of TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure (TC.0-TC.4); the general conjecture for arbitrary G is planned nowhere. Review: status changed from planned to missing. AG2.3 builds definite-unitary eigenvarieties and interpolated determinants, not Galois representations for the cohomology of a general locally symmetric space; for general G this is an assumption of the paper, which the Part II records with its assumption package.

items.name: The coadjoint motive
items.statement: Composing ρ_χ with the coadjoint representation ^LG → Aut(ĝ^*) gives Ad^*ρ_χ; it is conjectured to be motivic, i.e. there is a weight-zero motive M_coad over Q with H^*_ét(M_coad ×_Q Q̄, Q_p) ≅ Ad^*ρ_χ in degree 0. For simplicity M_coad is taken to be a Chow motive with coefficient field Q.
items.locator: Section 1.2.1, equation (6), pp. 5-6 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: MC.1 plans pure motives and Tate objects, so the category is planned; the coadjoint motive of an automorphic Galois representation is not.

items.name: Motivic cohomology and Scholl's integral subspace
items.statement: For a Chow motive M one has the bigraded motivic cohomology H^a_mot(M, Q(q)) after Voevodsky, with a comparison map to absolute étale cohomology; Scholl's theorem defines a natural subspace H^a_mot(M_Z, Q(q)) of classes that extend to a good model over Z. The case of interest is a = q = 1, giving H^1_mot((M_coad)_Z, Q(1)) → H^1_f(G_Q, Ad^*ρ_χ(1)).
items.locator: Section 1.2.2, equation (7), p. 6 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: MC.4 plans geometric mixed motives and motivic cohomology, and PS.3 the regulators and leading terms; Scholl's integral subspace and the comparison with Bloch–Kato f-cohomology are the specific inputs used here. Review note on status: Only partly planned: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.4 and PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.3 plan motivic cohomology and regulators, but Scholl's integral subspace H^a_mot(M_Z, Q(q)) (Scholl, Theorem 1.1.6) and its comparison with H^1_f are planned nowhere.

items.name: The Bloch–Kato and Beilinson expectations
items.statement: Conjecturally the map H^1_mot((M_coad)_Z, Q(1)) ⊗ Q_p → H^1_f(G_Q, Ad^*ρ_χ(1)) is an isomorphism (Bloch–Kato 5.3(ii)), and Beilinson's conjecture makes dim_Q of the source equal to the order of vanishing of L(s, Ad^*ρ_χ) at s = 0, which a Γ-factor computation shows is δ.
items.locator: Section 1.2.2, p. 6 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The Bloch–Kato assembly and the special-value conjectures are planned in PeriodsAndSpecialValues (PS.3 and PS.6); the numerical coincidence with δ is what makes the paper's conjecture plausible.

items.name: The motivic Q-lattice L and its dual
items.statement: L := H^1_mot((M_coad)_Z, Q(1)) is conjecturally a δ-dimensional Q-vector space with L ⊗ Q_p ≅ H^1_f(G_Q, Ad^*ρ_χ(1)); its Q-linear dual L^* then acts, after extension to Q_p, on the cohomology of Y(K) through the derived Hecke algebra.
items.locator: Section 1.2.2, equations (8)-(9), p. 6; Section 1.3, pp. 7-8 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The object whose hidden rational action is the subject of the central conjecture.

items.name: The reciprocity law: derived Hecke operators indexed by Galois cohomology
items.statement: Expected in general after tensoring with Q_p: T-tilde (x) Q_p = T (x) Lambda^* H^1_f(G_Q, Ad^* rho_chi(1))^* (x) Q_p (13), an indexing of derived Hecke operators by Galois cohomology. Proved in the setting of Sections 6-8 (T_{K_0,m} = Z_p): V = H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1))^dual acts, Lambda^* V embeds in the strict algebra (Theorem 8.5), and if H^q(Y(1), Z_p)_m = Z_p the image of T-tilde in End H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m equals Lambda^* V integrally (Proposition 8.6).
items.locator: Section 1.3, equation (13), p. 7, with the Remark on p. 8; proved as Theorem 8.5 and Proposition 8.6 (Sections 8.26-8.27, pp. 96-98) (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The 'reciprocity law' of the title of Section 8: it relates the derived Hecke action to the Galois representation directly. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Locator: equation (13), not (1.3.1). 'Proved in Section 8.24' repeats a cross-reference slip in the paper: Section 8.24 is 'Dependence of our construction on choices', and the construction is in Sections 8.26-8.27 (see issues). The paper proves (13) only when T = Z_p, and then integrally.

items.name: The central conjecture
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 8.5. Let M_coad be the motive with Q-coefficients attached to Pi and the coadjoint representation of the dual group (assumed to exist with Q-coefficients), and assume the regulator H^1_mot(Q, M_coad,Z(1)) -> H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)) (x) Q_p is an isomorphism. Let V_{Q_p} = V (x) Q_p and V_Q the elements of V_{Q_p} whose pairing with motivic cohomology is Q-valued. Then, for the action of Lambda^* V_{Q_p} on H^*(Y(1), Q_p)_Pi given by Theorem 8.5, V_Q preserves H^*(Y(1), Q)_Pi.
items.locator: Section 1.3, p. 8; Conjecture 8.8, Section 8.7, p. 81 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The point of the paper: a hidden action of the motivic lattice on rational cohomology, computable p-adically through derived Hecke operators. Evidence: the coherent-cohomology analogue with Harris (numerically tested for weight-one forms), the archimedean analogue with Prasanna, the computations of Section 5, and the case of tori in Section 9. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Correct in substance. The printed conjecture is stated in the setting of Theorem 8.5, assumes M_coad descends to Q-coefficients and that the regulator from integral motivic cohomology to H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)) (x) Q_p is an isomorphism, and is phrased for V_Q.

items.name: The explicit hyperbolic three-manifold picture
items.statement: G = Res_{F/Q} PGL_2, F imaginary quadratic with odd class number, so that at full level Y(K) is H^3/PGL_2(O). For a prime q of O prime to p and alpha: F_q^* -> Z/p^n, regard alpha as <alpha> in H^1(Gamma_0(q), Z/p^n) via (a b; c d) -> a/d. The degree +1 derived Hecke operator T_{q,alpha} (14) is the composite H^1(PGL_2(O)) -> H^1(Gamma_0(q)) (pullback by pi_1), cup with <alpha>, then H^2(Gamma_0(q)) -> H^2(PGL_2(O)) (pushforward by pi_2), with Z/p^n coefficients; without the cup product it is the usual T_q. Its relation to the diamond operators of the Taylor-Wiles method is Koszul duality for the action of F_q^*.
items.locator: Section 1.4, equation (14), pp. 8-10 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The concrete model of the whole theory, and the natural first target for any formalisation. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Locator wrong in both versions: the hyperbolic three-manifold explication, with the relation to Taylor-Wiles and Koszul duality, is Section 1.4. Section 1.5 is the reciprocity-law explication ((15)-(16) and the Claim on p. 12).

items.name: The invariant-function model of the derived Hecke algebra
items.statement: H(G,U)_S is isomorphic to the algebra of assignments h: (x,y) in G/U x G/U -> h(x,y) in H^*(G_xy, S) (continuous cohomology of the profinite pointwise stabiliser) that are G-invariant ([g]^* h(gx,gy) = h(x,y)) and supported on finitely many G-orbits, with pointwise S-module structure and product (h_1*h_2)(x,z) = sum over G_xz-orbits O in G/U of Cores^{G_xz}_{G_{x y_0 z}}( h_1(x,y_0) cup h_2(y_0,z) ), for any y_0 in O (22)-(23). If a compact Delta fixes every point of G/U, restriction to Delta gives h_Delta: G/U x G/U -> H^*(Delta) with (h h')_Delta(x,z) = sum over y of h_Delta(x,y) cup h'_Delta(y,z) (24).
items.locator: Section 2.3, equations (22)-(24) and the Remark, pp. 16-17; identified with Definition 2.2 in Section A.11, pp. 110-112 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The model in which every later computation is made; it is the derived analogue of the description of the Hecke algebra by invariant functions. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The product is not a plain sum over y in G/U, which is infinite. The printed rule (22)-(23) groups the y into orbits O of G_xz; for each orbit it restricts h(x,y_0) and h'(y_0,z) to G_{x y_0 z}, cups them, and corestricts to G_xz; only finitely many orbits contribute. The value h(x,y) lies in H^*(G_xy, S), where G_xy is the pointwise stabiliser of (x,y). The simple rule (24) holds only after restriction to a compact Delta that fixes every point of G/U.

items.name: The double-coset model
items.statement: With U_x = U cap Ad(g_x)U the stabiliser in U of x = g_x U, and [U\G/U] a set of representatives, there is an isomorphism of S-modules, the sum over x in [U\G/U] of H^*(U_x, S) -> H(G,U) (25), sending alpha in H^*(U_z, S) to the G-invariant function h_{z,alpha} that vanishes off the G-orbit of (z, eU) and takes the value alpha at (z, eU).
items.locator: Section 2.4, equation (25), pp. 17-18; Section A.8, equations (182)-(183), pp. 107-108 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The basis in which derived Hecke operators are exhibited and in which the action on cohomology is computed. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: (25) is an isomorphism of S-modules only; the multiplication is computed through the model of Section 2.3.

items.name: Derived invariants and the action on them
items.statement: For a complex M of smooth G-modules, the derived U-invariants are RHom_{SG}(S[G/U], M) in D(Mod_S), represented by Hom_{SG}(P, M); H(G,U) acts on their cohomology on the right (26). With V as in (20), they are isomorphic to RHom_{S[U/V]}(S, M^V) (27), so their cohomology is the hypercohomology H^*(U/V, M^V) of the finite group U/V acting on the termwise invariants.
items.locator: Section 2.5, equations (26)-(27), pp. 18-19; Section A.9, p. 108 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: SR.0:derived-extension plans the derived extension of the smooth category, where this action belongs. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: M may be any complex of smooth G-modules; the action is a right action; the derived invariants are computed as H^*(U/V, M^V), not simply 'H^*(U, M)'.

items.name: The action on the cohomology of an arithmetic manifold
items.statement: Write K = K^(v) x K_v and C^*(U_v) for the S-cochains of Y(K^(v) x U_v) (28). Then M = lim over U_v of C^*(U_v) is a complex of smooth G_v-modules, M^{V_v} = C^*(V_v), and C^*(Y(K)) -> Hom_{S[K_v/V_v]}(S, C^*(V_v)) is a quasi-isomorphism, so C^*(Y(K)) is the derived K_v-invariants of M and (26) gives a right action of H(G_v, K_v)_S on H^*(Y(K), S), with Ext^i raising degree by i. Separately, (29)-(30) define H^*(K_v, S) -> H^*(Y(K), S) by pulling back along Y(K) -> B(K_v/K_{v,1}) for the covering Y(K_1) -> Y(K).
items.locator: Section 2.6, equation (28) and the Remark, pp. 19-20; Section 2.7, equations (29)-(30), pp. 20-21 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The construction that makes the algebra act on the objects of interest. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The print does not restrict v to places outside the level: for any v, with S finite and p_v invertible in S, H_v acts. The congruence-class map (29) is Section 2.7. Review note on status: Partly planned: the colimit M as a smooth G_v-module is CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.1 ('Torsion colimits and the smooth group action'), and Hecke correspondences on complexes are ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.3. The derived Hecke action is missing, as marked.

items.name: Hecke-trivial classes
items.statement: A class h in H^*(Y(K), S) is Hecke-trivial if for every place v not dividing the level of K with residue characteristic invertible on S, and every Hecke operator T supported at v, (T - deg T)^n h = 0 for some n = n(T). H^*(Y(K), S)_triv denotes the submodule of Hecke-trivial classes.
items.locator: Definition 2.9, Section 2.9, p. 22 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The trivial summand of the cohomology, whose derived Hecke module structure is the subject of Section 5. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Numbered Definition 2.9 in both v3 and print, not 2.8 (Lemma 2.8 is the Hecke-triviality of congruence classes, which is not an item). The definition also names H^*(Y(K), S)_triv.

items.name: Explicit form of the action of a derived Hecke operator
items.statement: With K_z = K ∩ Ad(g_z)K and ⟨α⟩ the image of α under H^*(K_v ∩ Ad(g_z)K_v) → H^*(Y(K_z), S), the action of the generator h_{z,α} on H^*(Y(K), S) is the composite of the pullback [g_z]^* : H^*(Y(K)) → H^*(Y(K_z)), cup product with ⟨α⟩, and the pushforward H^*(Y(K_z)) → H^*(Y(K)).
items.locator: Lemma 2.11, Section 2.10, equation (31), pp. 22-23; proof via Lemma A.10, p. 109 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The formula 'pull back, cup with a cohomology class of the level group, push forward' that makes derived Hecke operators computable; it is the statement a formalisation would target first. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Numbered Lemma 2.11 in both versions, not 2.10. Statement otherwise correct.

items.name: Change of coefficients and the passage to the p-adic limit
items.statement: For a ring map S -> S', the derived tensor product carries S[G_v/K_v] to S'[G_v/K_v] and induces an algebra map H_{v,S} -> H_{v,S'} compatible with the actions on H^*(Y(K), S) -> H^*(Y(K), S') (Section 2.12). The mod l^n algebras T-tilde_n form an inverse system whose limit acts on H^*(Y(K), Z_l) with image T-tilde (Section 2.13); restricting the pairs (v, n) used gives T-tilde(V) and the strict algebra (Section 2.14).
items.locator: Sections 2.12, 2.13 and 2.14, pp. 24-27 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The limit process that turns mod-p^n operators into p-adic ones. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Section numbers are 2.12 (change of coefficients), 2.13 (passage to l-adic coefficients) and 2.14 (restricted and strict algebras) in both versions, not 2.11-2.13.

items.name: Torus localisation setting
items.statement: Setting of Section 3: G is a split group over the nonarchimedean local field F_v, with a split model over O_v; K_v = G(O_v); A is a maximal split torus and B a Borel subgroup, both extending over O_v; S = Z/l^r with l^r | q_v - 1 and l prime to |W|. X_* = Hom(G_m, A) embeds in G_v/K_v by chi -> chi(varpi_v) (38); the reduction A_v cap K_v -> A(F_v) (residue field) splits uniquely by a Teichmuller lift (39), which induces an isomorphism on Z/l^r-cohomology; and G_v = K_v A_v K_v (Cartan). The derived Hecke algebra of (G_v, K_v) is compared with that of (A_v, A_v cap K_v) by restriction in the model of Section 2.3.
items.locator: Sections 3.1-3.2, equations (38)-(39), pp. 28-29 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The setting of the derived Satake isomorphism. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong: no Hecke algebra is localised here. 'Torus localisation' means the Smith-theory fixed-point method.

items.name: The derived Satake isomorphism
items.statement: In the setting of Section 3.2 (G split over F_v with split model over O_v, K_v = G(O_v), S = Z/l^r with l^r | q_v - 1, l prime to |W|), restriction in the model of Section 2.3 (restrict to A_v/(A_v cap K_v) = X_* in G_v/K_v and pull classes back along A_xy -> G_xy) is an algebra isomorphism from H(G_v, K_v)_S onto H(A_v, A_v cap K_v)_S^W (40), and the target is (S[X_*] (x) H^*(A(F_v), S))^W (41). In particular H(G_v, K_v)_S is graded commutative.
items.locator: Theorem 3.3, equations (40)-(41), pp. 29-30; proof in Section 3.11, pp. 34-35 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The main local theorem: it produces the 'nice primes' at which the global algebra is under control. SR.4 plans the classical Satake isomorphism for spherical representations, which is the degree-zero part of this statement. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Omits the hypotheses of Section 3.2 (G split with a split model over O_v, K_v = G(O_v), A a maximal split torus extending over O_v) and the identification (41) of the target. Graded commutativity is stated as a consequence on p. 28.

items.name: Roots are non-trivial on the relevant subgroups
items.statement: In the setting of Section 3.2, every nontrivial root alpha of A on G is nontrivial on the l-Sylow subgroup of A_v cap K_v; in particular alpha induces a nontrivial character A(F_v) -> F_v^* (F_v the residue field).
items.locator: Lemma 3.6, Section 3.5, p. 30 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: One of the structural lemmas behind Theorem 3.3. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague: 'the relevant compact subgroup' and 'consequences used to control the localisation' are not the printed statement.

items.name: Finite-field lemmas for the localisation
items.statement: Lemma 3.7: if G is split over the finite field F_v with q_v = 1 mod l^r and l does not divide |W|, then restriction H^*(G(F_v), Z/l^r) -> H^*(A(F_v), Z/l^r)^W is an isomorphism. Lemma 3.8: if G_1, G_2 are finite groups and M is a G_1 x G_2-module on which G_2 acts trivially and whose order is killed by #G_2, then corestriction H^*(G_1, M) -> H^*(G_1 x G_2, M) is zero.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.7 and 3.8, p. 31 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The computations with H^*(G(F_q)) and H^*(T(F_q)) on which the localisation argument rests. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague; the exact statements are needed. Lemma 3.8 differs between v3 and print: v3 omits the hypothesis that G_2 acts trivially on M, without which the lemma is false (see issues, fixed in print).

items.name: Double centraliser and splitness lemmas
items.statement: Lemma 3.9: let Gamma in G_v be a finite l-subgroup and S its double centraliser, as an algebraic F_v-subgroup of G. Then (a) the component group of S has order prime to l, and (b) the maximal compact subgroup S(F_v)^o fixes every point of G_v/K_v that Gamma fixes. Lemma 3.10: if z in G_v/K_v is not in the image of X_* (38), Gamma is an l-Sylow subgroup of A_v cap K_v and Gamma_z the stabiliser of z in Gamma, then corestriction H^*(Gamma_z) -> H^*(Gamma) is zero with Z/l^r coefficients. Section 3.11 deduces Theorem 3.3: bijectivity from Lemma 3.7 applied to the Levi centralising a, and multiplicativity from Lemma 3.10.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.9 and 3.10, pp. 32-34; Section 3.11, pp. 34-35 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The algebraic input that makes the restriction map an isomorphism onto the W-invariants. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Vague; the lemmas are not 'double centraliser' and 'splitness' statements 'for the relevant modules'.

items.name: The Iwahori–Hecke algebra and its centre
items.statement: Setting of Section 4.1: S = Z/l^r, q_v = 1 mod l^r, l prime to |W|, G split, I_v an Iwahori subgroup in K_v in good position with respect to A, and [K_v : I_v] = |W| mod l^r. H_I := End_{SG_v}(S[G_v/I_v]) is anti-isomorphic to the convolution algebra of functions on I_v\G_v/I_v (47) and isomorphic to S[W-tilde], W-tilde = X_* semidirect W (50); e_K = 1_{K_v}/meas(K_v) corresponds to (1/|W|) times the sum of w in W. H_K, H_IK = Hom_{SG_v}(S[G_v/K_v], S[G_v/I_v]) and H_KI = Hom_{SG_v}(S[G_v/I_v], S[G_v/K_v]) are identified with functions on double cosets (48), H_IK taking I-invariants to K-invariants. Z := S[X_*]^W maps isomorphically onto the centre of H_I and onto H_K (z -> e_K z), compatibly with the bimodule structures.
items.locator: Sections 4.1-4.3, equations (47)-(50), pp. 36-38 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The classical structure theory used to compare level 1 and level Γ_0(q) cohomology, and to localise the derived Iwahori–Hecke algebra. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: No Bernstein presentation and no discriminant element appear. The key structural fact is that for q_v = 1 in S the Iwahori-Hecke algebra is the group algebra of the affine Weyl group (50), via the Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation specialised at q = 1.

items.name: Morita equivalence after étale localisation
items.statement: Setting of Section 4.1 (G split over F_v, S = Z/l^r, q_v = 1 mod l^r, l prime to |W|). Let m be a maximal ideal of Z = S[X_*]^W over which Z -> S[X_*] is etale, and write H'_K = H_K (x)_Z Z_m and similarly H'_I, H'_IK, H'_KI. Then the bimodules H'_IK and H'_KI induce mutually inverse equivalences between the categories of H'_K-modules and H'_I-modules.
items.locator: Lemma 4.5, Section 4.4, pp. 38-39 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The Morita statement that transports cohomology at Iwahori level to cohomology at level 1; it is used in Section 6.5. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Add the hypotheses of Section 4.1 (S = Z/l^r, q_v = 1 mod l^r, l prime to |W|, G split). Both versions note Schneider's correction restricting the lemma to the etale locus.

items.name: Compatibility of the localisation maps
items.statement: Setting of Section 3.2. Restriction to W-tilde (identify w with wI_v) and restriction of classes to T = A(F_v) defines maps H_II -> functions W-tilde x W-tilde -> H^*(T,S) (54) and H_IK -> functions W-tilde x X_* -> H^*(T,S) (55) (similarly for H_KI), the targets carrying the convolution product sum over z in W-tilde of H_1(x,z) cup H_2(z,y). Then (54) is an algebra morphism, and (55) is compatible with (54) and with the products H_II x H_IK -> H_IK; similarly for H_KI.
items.locator: Section 4.6, maps (54)-(55), Lemma 4.7, pp. 40-41 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The derived version of the localisation, needed to move derived Hecke operators between Iwahori and spherical level. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The maps are (54) and (55); no equations (4.4.1) or (4.4.2) exist in either version. The derived Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_I := Ext^*_{SG_v}(S[G_v/I_v], S[G_v/I_v]) and the derived bimodules H_IK, H_KI are defined in Section 4.6.

items.name: The trivial representation is cyclic over the derived Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let D be a division algebra of dimension d^2 over an imaginary quadratic field F, G the group of norm-one elements of D, and K contained in the stabiliser of a maximal order (so Y(K) is compact of dimension d^2 - 1). For all but finitely many primes l, T-tilde preserves H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_triv, and (i) H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_triv is cyclic over T-tilde, generated by the trivial class; (ii) the image T-tilde_triv of T-tilde in End H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_triv is graded commutative, and T-tilde_triv (x) Q_l is the Q_l-algebra generated by H^*(Y(K), Q)_triv acting on itself by cup product.
items.locator: Theorem 5.2, p. 42 (setting in Section 5.1, p. 41) (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The first case in which generation in minimal degree is proved, and the one that suggests the rational form of the conjecture: the derived Hecke action is, rationally, cup product with classes of the arithmetic manifold. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Omits the setting of Section 5.1.

items.name: Surjectivity of pullback from congruence quotients
items.statement: For G arising from a division algebra over an imaginary quadratic field F and all sufficiently large ℓ: for each n there are infinitely many places v of F with q_v ≡ 1 mod ℓ^n at which the division algebra is split, such that the pullback H^*(G(F_v), Z/ℓ) → H^*(Y(K), Z/ℓ)_triv is surjective.
items.locator: Lemma 5.3, p. 42; proof in Sections 5.5-5.11, pp. 44-53 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The geometric heart of Theorem 5.2; the proof uses Quillen's computation of the cohomology of finite groups of Lie type together with a Chebotarev argument. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Statement correct (G(F_v) is the finite group of residue-field points). Its proof has a gap in the Chebotarev step of Section 5.11 (see issues).

items.name: The inputs to Lemma 5.3
items.statement: Section 5.4: Lemma 5.3 implies Theorem 5.2 (commutant argument (56)). Section 5.5 recalls: invariant forms on U_N give H^*(GL_N(O_F), C) in low degree (57) (Borel), with primitive generators Omega_1, Omega_3, ..., stability of homology (van der Kallen), and H^*(Y(K), C)_triv = H^*(SU_d, C) (59); Borel's and Quillen's computations of K-theory. Section 5.6 lists the constraints (i)-(vi) on l. Section 5.8 embeds Y(K) -> B(GL_N(O_F)) and formulates (a) a_i in K_i(O_F) has nonzero image in K_i(F_v)/l; (b) <xi_i, [b_i]^(N)> != 0; (c) the cup product of the xi_i pairs nontrivially with the Pontryagin product of the [b_i]; (d) iota_*[Y(K)] = M.([a_3]*...*[a_{2d-1}])^(N) with M in Q^* (62); and shows (a)-(d) imply Lemma 5.3. (d) is proved in 5.9, (b)-(c) in 5.10, (a) in 5.11.
items.locator: Sections 5.4-5.11, pp. 43-53 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Quillen's computation of the K-theory and cohomology of finite fields is an input the atlas touches only through ArithmeticKTheory's use of it for finite generation. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Misattributes the steps. (a), not (d), is the Chebotarev argument (Section 5.11). (d) is verified in Section 5.9 by Borel's invariant forms and the nonvanishing of the Borel regulator. (b) and (c) are verified in Section 5.10 by Quillen's Chern classes, Quillen's coproduct formula and Soule's Chern-class surjectivity. Section 5.5 uses Borel's stable cohomology and van der Kallen's homological stability; no 'Friedlander' comparison appears. Review note on status: Partly planned rather than missing: Quillen's finite-field K-theory is KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.1, Borel's stable cohomology and regulator classes are BorelRegulators:R.3-R.4 (invariant forms at AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1a). Soule's etale Chern classes and van der Kallen stability are planned nowhere.

items.name: The global assumptions
items.statement: (1) F = Q and G is a split, simply connected, semisimple Q-group with Borel B and maximal torus A. (2) Base level K_0, Y(1) = Y(K_0). (3) Pi is a tempered cohomological cuspidal automorphic representation with Pi^{K_0} != 0. (4) T_{K_0} is the Z_p-algebra generated by the prime-to-level, prime-to-p Hecke operators acting on the Z_p-chain complex of Y(K_0) in the derived category. (5) Pi has coefficient field Q, giving T_{K_0} -> Z_p (73). (6) T is the set of places where Pi is ramified or K_0 is not hyperspecial. (7) k = Z/p, p > 5, with (a) H^*(Y(K_0), Z) p-torsion-free, (b) p prime to |W| and p not in T, (c) with chi: T_{K_0} -> Z_p -> k and m = ker chi (74): T_{K_0,m} = Z_p (75) and H_j(Y(1), Z_p)_m = 0 for j outside [q, q+delta] (76). (8) S = T union {p}.
items.locator: Section 6.1, items (1)-(8), equations (73)-(76), and the Remark, pp. 53-55 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The standing hypotheses of Theorems 7.6 and 8.5. They are the Calegari–Geraghty-type assumptions; the atlas plans the corresponding commutative algebra but not this package. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Printed as items (1)-(8) with 7(a)-(c), not conditions (a)-(g). 7(c) is the no-congruence hypothesis (75)-(76), not a largeness condition on the image (big image is Section 6.2(b)). The item also omits: G simply connected, semisimple and split over Q; coefficient field of Pi equal to Q; p > 5; p-torsion-freeness 7(a). The Remark's proof of 7(c) treats compact inner forms of SL_n, which are excluded by (1) (see issues).

items.name: Galois-theoretic assumptions and the deformation ring
items.statement: For deeper levels K in K_0 and characters T_K -> k-bar there are Galois representations Gal(Q-bar/Q) -> G^dual(k-bar) with unramified compatibility, and for m there is rho-tilde: Gal(Q-bar/Q) -> G^dual(T_{K,m}) with (a) unramified compatibility: tr(tau o rho-tilde)(Frob_q) is the Satake Hecke operator T_{q,tau} for q outside the level; (b) big image: rho-bar restricted to Gal(Q-bar/Q(zeta_{p^inf})) contains the image of the k-points of the simply connected cover of G^dual; (c) rho-tilde is crystalline at p; (d) local-global compatibility at Taylor-Wiles primes dividing the level and at Iwahori level Y_0(q); (e) H^0(Q_q, Ad rho-bar) = H^2(Q_q, Ad rho-bar) = 0 for all q in S, so local deformation rings are Z_p at q in T and formally smooth at p. This yields rho: Gal -> G^dual(Z_p) (77); R_rhobar is the universal crystalline deformation ring of rho-bar unramified outside S.
items.locator: Section 6.2, (a)-(e) and (77), pp. 56-57 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Global deformation rings with their tangent spaces and Taylor–Wiles data are planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 and in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2; the specific assumption package is the paper's own. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Too vague about the assumption package; the minimal-level condition is (e). Review note on status: The cited stages are reasonable suppliers of generic deformation theory; the crystalline (Fontaine-Laffaille) local condition is LocalGaloisDeformationRings:L7. The assumption package itself is the paper's own and is not planned.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles primes and auxiliary level structures
items.statement: A Taylor-Wiles prime of level n is a prime q not dividing the level of K_0 with p^n | q - 1 and rho-bar(Frob_q) conjugate to a strongly regular element of T^dual(k) (centraliser in G^dual equal to T^dual). For a fixed large s, a Taylor-Wiles datum of level n is Q_n = (q_1, ..., q_s) with strongly regular Frob^T_{q_i} in T^dual(k) conjugate to rho-bar(Frob_{q_i}) and p^n | q_i - 1; R = rs with r = rank A (78). Y_0(q) and Y_1(q) add Iwahori and pro-unipotent level at q (79); Y_1(q,n) is the subcover of Y_1(q) -> Y_0(q) with group A(F_q)/p^n (80); Y_1^*(Q_n) is the fibre product of the Y_1(q_i, n) over Y(1), Galois over Y_0(Q_n) with group T_n = product of A(F_q)/p^n = (Z/p^n)^R (81)-(82).
items.locator: Section 6.3, equations (78)-(82), pp. 57-58 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Taylor–Wiles primes and the auxiliary level structures are planned at GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5; what is new here is the use of their derived Hecke operators. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Omits that a Taylor-Wiles datum has a fixed cardinality s (chosen once and large), carries chosen strongly regular elements Frob^T_{q_i}, and consists of primes not dividing the level of K_0.

items.name: Rings of diamond operators
items.statement: S_n = Z/p^n[T_n] and S'_n = Z_p[T_n] (83), acting on the chains of Y_1^*(Q_n) by deck transformations; choosing T_n = (Z/p^n)^R, S_n = Z/p^n[x_1, ..., x_R]/((1+x_i)^{p^n} - 1) with x_i = [e_i] - 1 (84), and S := Z_p[[x_1, ..., x_R]] (85) surjects onto S_n compatibly with the augmentations (kernels I and I_n).
items.locator: Section 6.4, equations (83)-(85), p. 59 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: P8 plans exactly this: patching from systems (R_N, S_N, C_N) with S_N a finite quotient of O[Δ_N], and the construction of S_∞. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The group is T_n = product over q in Q_n of A(F_q)/p^n, of rank R = rs, not a product of (F_q^*)(p).

items.name: Passing to the limit in the Ext-algebras of the diamond rings
items.statement: The change-of-rings map Ext^*_{S_n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) → Ext^*_{S_∞/p^n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) is surjective, and the map Ext^*_{S_∞/p^n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) → Ext^*_{S_∞}(Z_p, Z/p^n) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Lemma (unnumbered), Section 6.4, maps (86)-(87), pp. 59-60 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The algebraic step that lets the derived Hecke action at finite level be compared with the exterior algebra appearing in the limit. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Correct; in print the lemma is unnumbered (the label 'toinfinity' is from the source file).

items.name: Comparison of level 1 and level Γ_0(q) cohomology
items.statement: Let q be a prime not dividing the level of K_0 with q = 1 mod p^n, S = Z/p^n, and assume local-global compatibility at Y_0(q) (H_K, as the centre of H_I, acts on H_*(Y_0(q), k)_m through the eigencharacter of Pi). If rho-bar(Frob_q) is conjugate to a strongly regular element of T^dual(k), then the maps H^*(Y(1),S) (x)_{H_K} H_KI -> H^*(Y_0(q),S) and H^*(Y_0(q),S) (x)_{H_I} H_IK -> H^*(Y(1),S) of (91) become isomorphisms after localising at a maximal ideal of H_K induced by m; in particular H^*(Y_0(q), Z/p^n)_m = H^*(Y(1), Z/p^n)_m (x)_{H_K} H_KI (92).
items.locator: Lemma 6.6, Section 6.5, maps (91)-(92), pp. 61-62 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The Morita-style comparison of Lemma 4.5 applied to arithmetic manifolds; it is what allows derived Hecke operators at q to be computed at level 1. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Add the hypotheses of Section 6.5 (q does not divide the level of K_0 and q = 1 mod p^n) and the first assertion: the maps (91) become isomorphisms after localising at a maximal ideal of H_K induced by m.

items.name: Eigenvalues at Iwahori level and the doubling projection
items.statement: For q part of a Taylor–Wiles datum, all generalised eigenvalues of k[X_*^+] on H^*(Y_0(q), k)_m are of the form χ_{Frob^T} with Frob^T ∈ T^∨(k) conjugate to Frobenius at q (Corollary 6.7); moreover the χ_{Frob^T}-eigenspace of H^*(Y_0(q), Z/p^n)_m is isomorphic to H^*(Y(1), Z/p^n)_m, with pushforward and (projected) pullback as mutually inverse maps.
items.locator: Corollary 6.7 and the Remark after it, equations (95)-(96), p. 63 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The explicit identification used to transport classes between the two levels.

items.name: Cohomological vanishing at auxiliary level
items.statement: For q part of a Taylor–Wiles datum of level n and under the standing assumptions, the homology H_j(Y_1(q, n), Z_p)_m vanishes outside the expected range [q, q + δ] (Lemma 6.9); and every generalised eigenvalue of k[𝒳̃_*^+] on H_*(Y_1(q,n), k)_m is one of the eigenvalues on H_*(Y_0(q), k)_m (Lemma 6.10).
items.locator: Lemma 6.9, p. 64; Lemma 6.10 and the splitting (98), p. 65 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The vanishing that makes the patched complex have amplitude δ, which is the technical heart of the Calegari–Geraghty method. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Statements correct. The proof of Lemma 6.9 cites the wrong assumption (see issues).

items.name: Deformations at Taylor–Wiles primes are toral
items.statement: Let q be a Taylor–Wiles prime of level n and assume ρ̄|G_{Q_q} is unramified with image in T^∨. Then any deformation of ρ̄|G_{Q_q} can be conjugated into T^∨, and in particular factors through the abelianisation G_{Q_q}^{ab}.
items.locator: Lemma 6.12, Section 6.11, pp. 66-67 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The local deformation computation that produces the diamond operators and identifies the tangent space at q.

items.name: Chain complexes at level Q_n and the patched limit
items.statement: For a datum Q_n: R_{Q_n} is the deformation ring at level S union Q_n and R_n its quotient of inertial level <= n at Q_n (102), with S_n -> R_n/p^n (103) compatible with deck transformations (local-global compatibility). The Z/p^n-chains of Y_1^*(Q_n) are a complex of finite free S_n-modules, cut down to a perfect complex C_n computing H_*(Y_1^*(Q_n), Z/p^n)_{m,Frob^T} (109) with H^* Hom_{S_n}(C_n, Z/p^n) = H^*(Y_0(Q_n), Z/p^n)_{m,Frob^T} (110), the Ext^*_{S_n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) = H^*(T_n)-action being cup product via Y_0(Q_n) -> BT_n (107)-(108). Lemma 7.2: H_j(Y_1^*(Q_n), Z_p)_m = 0 for j outside [q, q+delta]. After passing to a subsequence (Section 7.3): a complex C of finite free S-modules with C (x)_S S_n = C_n (111); R = Z_p[[x_1, ..., x_{R-delta}]] with S -> R, R -> R-bar_n, R ->> R_rhobar compatible (113) and R (x)_S S_n = R_n (114); an R-action on H_*(C); H^*(Hom_S(C, Z_p)) = H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m (115); and, using 6.2(e), C has homology only in degree q, free over R, with R (x)_S Z_p = R_rhobar = image of T_{K_0} (116).
items.locator: Section 7.1, Lemma 7.2 and (101)-(110), pp. 69-71; Section 7.3 (a)-(g), (111)-(116), pp. 71-72 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: This is exactly the construction P8 plans — patching complexes with cohomology in several degrees, the ultrapatching limit, the augmentation isomorphism and the comparison of finite-level Hecke actions — together with P7's perfect complexes and derived coefficient change and R03.5's patching modules. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Refine: the finite-level complexes have Z/p^n coefficients and are cut down to the chosen Frob^T summand; the comparison is C (x)_S S_n = C_n, not C_inf (x)^L Z_p = C.

items.name: Straightening the map S_∞ → R_∞
items.statement: One can choose generators so that S_∞ = Z_p[[x_1, …, x_R]] and R_∞ = Z_p[[y_1, …, y_{R−δ}]], with the x_i and y_j in the kernels of the compatible augmentations to Z_p, and the map S_∞ → R_∞ given by x_i ↦ y_i for i ≤ R − δ and x_i ↦ 0 otherwise.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5, Section 7.4, p. 73 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The normal form that exhibits the patched complex as a Koszul complex on δ variables, from which the exterior algebra action comes. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): Statement correct; the proof has an index misprint (see issues).

items.name: Generation in minimal degree
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Sections 6.1 and 6.2, the cohomology H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m is generated, as a module over the strict global derived Hecke algebra, by its minimal degree component H^{q}(Y(1), Z_p)_m.
items.locator: Theorem 7.6, pp. 74-75 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The second, and main, case of the generation statement; it says that the derived Hecke algebra accounts for the whole of the cohomology in the Taylor–Wiles setting.

items.name: The coadjoint representation and the Selmer group
items.statement: Ad^*: G^dual -> GL(g-tilde) is the coadjoint representation on the Z-dual g-tilde of Lie(G^dual) (Section 8.1). For a Gal(Q_S/Q)-module M, H^1(Z[1/S], M) is its etale (Galois) cohomology and H^1_f(Z[1/S], M) the classes whose restriction to Q_p lies in the Fontaine-Laffaille subgroup H^1_f(Q_p, M) (Hodge weights in [-(p-3)/2, (p-3)/2]); under the paper's assumptions it equals the Bloch-Kato H^1_f(Q, M) (Section 8.3). V := Hom_{Z_p}(H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)), Z_p) (122).
items.locator: Section 8.1, p. 76; Sections 8.2-8.3, pp. 76-77; definition of V, (122), Section 8.4, p. 78 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Selmer groups with local conditions are planned in several roadmaps (for instance AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty NC.6 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology); the coadjoint Selmer group of an automorphic Galois representation, with the Bloch–Kato conditions used here, is the specific object. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: H^1_f(Z[1/S], M) imposes no condition at the primes of S other than p; V is defined directly as the Z_p-dual (122), and patching later identifies W = t_S/t_R with V (168). No equation (8.3.1) exists in either version. Review note on status: The cited stage is not a supplier: AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.6 is the anabelian reconstruction / Chabauty-Kim handoff. Selmer groups with local conditions are ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.5 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 and L4 (finite Bloch-Kato conditions); torsion Fontaine-Laffaille theory is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Review: planned stages corrected from AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.6 (anabelian reconstruction, not a supplier) to the Selmer-group and Fontaine–Laffaille owners.

items.name: Both sides are free of rank δ
items.statement: Both H^1_f(Z[1/Σ], Ad^*ρ(1)) and V are free Z_p-modules of rank δ.
items.locator: Lemma 8.9, Section 8.7, pp. 81-83 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The numerical match between the Galois side and the degree range of the cohomology; it is what makes the exterior algebra act with the right size. Review note on status: Missing as marked; its inputs (Poitou-Tate, global Euler characteristic and dual-Selmer numerics) are planned at ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 and R02.6.

items.name: The reciprocity law
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Section 6 there is a function a : Z_{≥1} → Z_{≥1} and an action of V_∞ on H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m by endomorphisms of degree +1 such that for every n ≥ 1 and every prime q ≡ 1 mod p^{a(n)} equipped with a strongly regular element of T^∨(k) conjugate to ρ̄(Frob_q), the two actions of H^1(T_q, Z/p^n) on H^*(Y(1), Z/p^n)_m — one through the patching map f_{q,n}, one through the derived Hecke operators ι_{q,n} — coincide. This property characterises the action uniquely. In particular the strict global derived Hecke algebra contains V, and the induced map ⋀^*V → End H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m is injective.
items.locator: Theorem 8.5, Section 8.4, pp. 78-79 (with (122)-(124)); proof in Section 8.26, pp. 96-98 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The main theorem of the paper: derived Hecke operators at Taylor–Wiles primes are indexed by Galois cohomology, compatibly for all such primes at once. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): The printed action is of V (not 'V_inf') on H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m, and the two actions are those of H^1(T_q, Z/p^n), T_q = A(F_q)/p^n, through f_{q,n} (124) and iota_{q,n} (123). The proof also gives freeness of H^* over Lambda^* V (p. 98), which is not an item.

items.name: When the derived Hecke algebra is exactly an exterior algebra
items.statement: If H^{q}(Y(1), Z_p)_m = Z_p, then the image of the full global derived Hecke algebra in End H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m coincides with the exterior algebra generated by V; in particular that image is graded commutative. The same conclusion holds more generally when there is a semisimple Q_p-algebra of degree-preserving endomorphisms of H^*(Y(1), Q_p) with the stated properties.
items.locator: Proposition 8.6 and the Remark after it, pp. 79-80; proof in Section 8.27, p. 98 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The statement that identifies 𝓗 with ⋀^*V, i.e. the integral form of the reciprocity law (1.3.1); it is also where graded commutativity is obtained in the cases of interest.

items.name: Convergent Taylor–Wiles data
items.statement: A sequence of Taylor–Wiles data Q_n of level n is convergent if the Q_n have the cohomological properties of Section 8.10(b) and one can pass to the limit in the sense of Section 7.3, i.e. the patched data R_∞, S_∞, C_∞, f_n, g_n exist with all the properties listed there.
items.locator: Definition 8.11, Section 8.10, p. 83 (condition (b) of Section 8.10 and (131)) (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The hypothesis under which the construction of the V-action is carried out.

items.name: Tangent spaces and the Galois-cohomological description of V_n
items.statement: t_R = Hom_*(R, Z_p[e]/e^2) injects into t_S with saturated image and W := t_S/t_R is free of rank delta (132). Lemma 8.14: R_{Q_n} -> R-bar_n induces an isomorphism on Hom_*(-, Z/p^n[e]/e^2). With t_{R_n}, t_{S_n} and W_n = coker(t_{R_n} -> t_{S_n}) (133), there are isomorphisms t_{R_n} = t_R/p^n, t_{S_n} = t_S/p^n and W_n = W/p^n (134). Also t_{S_n} = Ext^1_{S_n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) = H^1(T_n, Z/p^n) = the sum over q in Q_n of H^1(Q_q, Ad rho-bar_n)/H^1_ur (136)-(140), the last depending on the choice of Frob^T_q. There is a canonical surjection t_{S_n} ->> V/p^n (142), and for a convergent sequence it descends to W_n = V/p^n = Hom(H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)), Z/p^n) (143), via the perfect pairing (145).
items.locator: Sections 8.12-8.16, equations (132)-(147) with Lemma 8.14, pp. 83-88 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The chain of identifications that converts the patching variables into Galois cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Refine: there is no 'V_n'. What is identified is W_n = coker(t_{R_n} -> t_{S_n}), and Lemma 8.14 concerns R_{Q_n} -> R-bar_n, the Artinian quotient (112).

items.name: The injection of local Galois cohomology into the derived Hecke algebra
items.statement: For a Taylor-Wiles prime q of level n with chosen Frob^T_q and T_q = A(F_q)/p^n, the Satake isomorphism of Section 3 and the splitting (150) of S[X_*] completed at m-tilde give an isomorphism (H^(1)_q)_m -> S[X_*]_chi (x) H^1(T_q) (153), and theta(h) is the preimage of 1 (x) h (154); changing Frob^T_q by w twists theta by w. Lemma 8.18: theta(h) is the image of |W| e_K Theta (x) <h> (x) e_K under H_KI (x) H_I (x) H_IK -> H_K, where Theta in S[X_*] completed projects to 1 on the chi-factor and 0 on the others; that is, theta(h) acts by pullback to Y_0(q), projection to the Frob^T_q-eigenspace, cup with h, and pushforward (149). For a datum Q_n this gives iota_{Q_n}: t_{S_n} = H^1(T_n) -> the tensor product of the (H_q)_m (159)-(160). Lemma 8.20: if Q_n is a convergent sequence, then for each n the action of t_{S_n} on H^*(Y(1), Z/p^n)_m through iota_{Q_n} is trivial on the image of t_{R_n} and so factors through t_{S_n} -> W_n.
items.locator: Sections 8.17-8.20: (148)-(160), Lemma 8.18 (pp. 88-92) and Lemma 8.20 (pp. 92-93) (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The concrete link between Galois cohomology at q and derived Hecke operators at q. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: The injection lands in the m-completion (H^(1)_q)_m and is defined through the derived Satake isomorphism. Lemma 8.20 is not a factorisation of this injection through patching maps: it says that for a convergent sequence the t_{S_n}-action through iota_{Q_n} kills the image of t_{R_n}.

items.name: Strict sequences of Taylor–Wiles data and their properties
items.statement: Definition 8.22: a Taylor-Wiles datum Q_n of level n is strict if iota_{Q_n}: t_{S_n} -> End H^*(Y(1), Z/p^n)_m factors through f_{Q_n}: t_{S_n} ->> V/p^n; it then gives an action of V/p^n. Lemma 8.23: every member of a convergent sequence (Definition 8.11) is strict. The V/p^n-action does not depend on the choice of the Frob^T_q (163). Lemma 8.25: for two sequences Q_n, Q'_n of strict data there is a subsequence J such that for each k there is j_0 with the two V-actions on H^*(Y(1), Z/p^k)_m (from Q_j and Q'_j, reduced mod p^k) equal for all j in J, j >= j_0. Section 8.26: a sequence is V-convergent if its members are strict and the induced actions on H^*(Y(1), Z/p^k)_m are eventually constant for each k; such sequences exist, and all of them give the same action of V on H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m.
items.locator: Section 8.21, Definition 8.22 and Lemma 8.23, pp. 93-94; Section 8.24 with (163) and Lemma 8.25, pp. 94-96; Section 8.26, pp. 96-97 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The bookkeeping that shows the action produced by patching does not depend on the chosen Taylor–Wiles data; Section 8.24 discusses the residual dependence on choices. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Misstated. Definition 8.22 concerns a single datum, not a sequence, and strictness is factorisation through f_{Q_n}. Lemma 8.25 is an asymptotic statement along a subsequence, not the statement that two constructions agree.

items.name: The reciprocity law in the form of an indexing of derived Hecke operators
items.statement: Let q be unramified for rho with q = 1 mod p^n and rho-bar(Frob_q) conjugate to a strongly regular element of T^dual(k); let nu in X_*(A)^+ be strictly dominant and alpha in H^1(A(F_q), Z/p^n). Let T_{q,nu,alpha} be the derived Hecke operator with Z/p^n coefficients supported on the G_q-orbit of (nu K_q, K_q), with value there corresponding to alpha under H^*(K_q cap nu K_q nu^{-1}, Z/p^n) = H^*(A(F_q), Z/p^n). Let [q,nu,alpha] in V/p^n be the functional on H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)) given by local reciprocity against the pushforward of alpha along e_{nu,rho(Frob_q)}: Lie(T^dual) -> Ad rho (170). Then there is N_0(m) such that for q = 1 mod p^{N_0(m)} (and m <= n) the actions of T_{q,nu,alpha} and [q,nu,alpha] on H^*(Y(1), Z/p^m)_m coincide.
items.locator: Section 8.28 with Lemma 8.29 and (170), pp. 98-101 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The final assembly of the main theorem and the precise statement of the indexing (1.3.1). Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Misdescribed. Lemma 8.29 does not identify the strict algebra with T (x) Lambda^* H^1_f; that identification is Proposition 8.6 (item 50) and (13). Lemma 8.29 is the explicit reciprocity law for individual derived Hecke operators, and its printed statement mixes n and m (see issues).

items.name: Evidence from tori and the trivial representation
items.statement: Let T be an anisotropic torus over a number field F (so q = 0, delta = dim S, and Y(K) is a union of compact tori S/Delta, with Delta a congruence subgroup of T(O) of rank delta, free of p-torsion). Let M be the motive of H_1(T), with M_p = X_*(T) (x) Z_p(1) the p-adic Tate module; H^1(O[1/S], M_p) = T(O[1/S]) (x) Z_p (171); H^1_{f,ur}(F, M_p) corresponds to Delta' commensurable with Delta (x) Z_p (arranged to contain it). Assuming H^1_mot(M_Z, Q(1)) is the image of Delta (x) Q, V = H^1_{f,ur}(F, M_p)^dual = Hom(Delta', Z_p) acts on H^*(Y, Z_p) by cup product through H^1(Delta', Z_p) -> H^1(Delta, Z_p) (172). This action agrees with the derived Hecke formalism at places outside S, and the motivic lattice (classes Q-valued on Delta) preserves H^*(Y, Q).
items.locator: Section 1.3(iii), p. 8; Sections 9.1-9.2, pp. 101-103 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The paper's own evidence; the stronger evidence is external (the coherent-cohomology analogue with Harris, and the archimedean conjecture with Prasanna). Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Section 9 verifies Conjecture 8.8 for anisotropic tori only under an Assumption the author did not check (p. 102): the integral motivic cohomology H^1_mot(M_Z, Q(1)) is the image of Delta (x) Q. For Section 5 an analogous statement is only mentioned, not proved.

items.name: Models of the derived Hecke algebra and their identifications
items.statement: Appendix A ('Remedial algebra') constructs, in detail, the category of smooth modules with enough projectives, the modules S[G/U], induction and compact induction with Frobenius reciprocity, restriction of induced representations, the derived Hecke algebra in the Ext-model, the invariant-function model and the double-coset model, the action on derived invariants, and the multiplication rule in each model, proving that the identifications are compatible.
items.locator: Appendix A, Sections A.1-A.11 with Lemma A.10, pp. 104-112 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The careful foundations; SR.0:derived-extension and SR.1 are the layers where this belongs, and it is what a formalisation would have to do first. Review note on status: Partly planned: the smooth category and invariants are SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0, and compact induction, Frobenius reciprocity and Mackey filtrations are SR.2. The identifications of the models of the derived Hecke algebra (A.7-A.11) are missing, as marked.

items.name: Koszul-algebra computations
items.statement: Let B be a commutative ring, S = B[[x_1, ..., x_r]] -> R = B[[y_1, ..., y_{r-delta}]] with x_i -> y_i for i <= r - delta and x_i -> 0 otherwise, and t_S, t_R the B-duals of the cotangent spaces. Lemma B.1: Ext^*_S(B,B) is the free exterior algebra on its degree-1 part, Ext^*_S(B,B) = Lambda^* t_S, and Ext^*_S(R,B) = Lambda^*(t_S/t_R), the Ext^*_S(B,B)-action being induced by Lambda^* t_S -> Lambda^*(t_S/t_R). Section B.2: for R = Sym(W), W free of rank e, the Koszul resolution gives Ext^i_R(B,B) = (Lambda^i W)^dual, and Lambda^*(W^dual) -> Hom_R(K,K) (contractions) is a quasi-isomorphism of dgas; the same holds for power series. Lemma B.3: for U a free submodule of W with W/U free and R-bar = Sym(W/U), Ext^*_R(R-bar, B) = (Lambda^* U)^dual, and the action of Ext^*_R(B,B) = (Lambda^* W)^dual is the one induced by W^dual -> U^dual.
items.locator: Appendix B: Lemma B.1 and Section B.2, pp. 112-113; Lemma B.3, pp. 114-115 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The Koszul duality that turns the patched Koszul complex into an exterior algebra action; it is the algebraic explanation for the shape of the answer. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong. Ext^*_S(B,B) is exterior on all generators of t_S (rank = number of variables), not on delta generators; the rank-delta exterior algebra is Ext^*_S(R, B) = Lambda^*(t_S/t_R). Lemma B.5 is not a Koszul computation: it is the sheaf-versus-singular comparison of Section B.4 (item 59).

items.name: A topological lemma
items.statement: Let X -> Y be a Galois covering of pointed Hausdorff spaces with group Delta, and E a coefficient ring. The two actions of H^*(Delta, E) on H^*(Y, E) coincide: (a) pullback along the classifying map Y -> B Delta followed by cup product; (b) the Yoneda action through C^*(Y; E) = Hom_{E Delta}(C_*(X, E), E). The proof uses Lemma B.5, comparing singular and sheaf cohomology with products for a locally contractible Hausdorff space (valid as stated for A = E; see issues). This justifies the identification in (107) of the Ext^*_{S_n}(Z/p^n, Z/p^n) = H^*(T_n, Z/p^n)-action on H^*(Y_0(Q_n)) with cup product via Y_0(Q_n) -> BT_n.
items.locator: Section B.4 with Lemma B.5, pp. 115-116; used at Section 7.1, (107)-(108), p. 70 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: The link between group cohomology of the level subgroup and cohomology of the arithmetic manifold. Review (REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19): statement corrected against the published text: Wrong content and use. B.4 is not about pullback from congruence quotients (Section 2.7) or Section 5.

items.name: Ext-groups in an abelian category
items.statement: For objects X, Y of an abelian category, Ext^i(X, Y) is defined (by derived functors of Hom, or in the derived category), with the Yoneda product Ext^i(Y, Z) × Ext^j(X, Y) → Ext^{i+j}(X, Z) making ⊕_i Ext^i(X, X) a graded algebra.
items.locator: Definition 2.2, equation (21), p. 16; Section A.7, p. 107 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Mathlib has Ext in an abelian category, both the classical construction and the derived-category one; what is missing is the abelian category of smooth representations of a p-adic group in which these Ext-groups are taken.

items.name: Group cohomology and cup products
items.statement: For a group Γ and a Γ-module M, H^*(Γ, M) is the cohomology of the inhomogeneous cochain complex, with cup products; the classes α ∈ H^*(K_v ∩ Ad(g)K_v, S) appearing in the double-coset model of the derived Hecke algebra and the class ⟨α⟩ of Lemma 2.10 live in such groups.
items.locator: Sections 2.3-2.4, pp. 16-18; Lemma 2.11, p. 22; Section A.3, p. 105 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7; arXiv v3 has the same numbering)
items.note: Mathlib has group cohomology through inhomogeneous cochains with the low-degree API; the cohomology of the compact open subgroups appearing here, and the transfer/pushforward maps relating it to the cohomology of arithmetic manifolds, are not in the libraries. Review: status changed from library to planned. Mathlib at 082e2d3 has groupCohomology (inhomogeneous cochains) but no cup product on it, and Tau Ceti has only explicit low-degree cup products in continuous cohomology; ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 plans cup products in continuous cohomology and ALS.3 their compatibility with Hecke correspondences.

items.name: Congruence classes are Hecke-trivial
items.statement: Let h be in the image of H^*(K_v, S) -> H^*(Y(K), S) (29). For every prime w of F that does not divide the level of K or #S, with G(F_w) split, and every usual Hecke operator T supported at w, T h = deg(T) h.
items.locator: Lemma 2.8, Section 2.7, p. 21 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Key lemma: congruence classes are Hecke-trivial. Used in Lemma 5.3 and Section 5.8 ('by Lemma 2.8') and behind the commutation remark after Lemma 2.11. Not among the 61 items. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Cup products and commutation of derived Hecke operators
items.statement: (i) For alpha in H^*(K_v, S), cup product with the image of alpha under (29) is the action of h_{e,alpha} in H(G_v, K_v)_S (take g_z = 1 in Lemma 2.11). (ii) For places v != w, g_v in G_v, g_w in G_w and classes alpha_v in H^*(K_v cap Ad(g_v)K_v), alpha_w in H^*(K_w cap Ad(g_w)K_w), the composite of the two derived Hecke operators is push-pull along Y(K) <- Y(K_{g_v} cap K_{g_w}) -> Y(K) with cup product by alpha_v cup alpha_w in the middle; hence derived Hecke operators at different places graded-commute.
items.locator: Remarks after Lemma 2.11, Section 2.10, diagram (32), p. 23 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Proves that derived Hecke operators at different places graded-commute, which the strict algebra's graded commutativity (Section 2.14) and Section 5.4 rely on. Also that cup product with congruence classes is a derived Hecke operator, used in Section 5.4 and in the proof of Theorem 7.6 ('see the Remark in Section 2.10'). Route: the Part II.

items.name: Passage of generation from Z/l^m to Z_l coefficients
items.statement: Suppose that for all m <= n there are finite sets of primes Q_n = {q_1, ..., q_r} with l^n | q_i - 1 such that H^*(Y(K), Z/l^m) is generated, over the image of the tensor product of the H_{q_i, Z/l^m}, by elements of a fixed degree D. Then H^*(Y(K), Z_l) is generated over the global derived Hecke algebra T-tilde by elements of degree D. The same holds after localisation at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra.
items.locator: Section 2.13, (33)-(35) and (*), pp. 25-26 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The limit argument that turns mod l^m generation into Z_l generation. It ends the proof of Theorem 7.6 ('Passing to the limit (as in the discussion of Section 2.13)') and is not an item. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Preservation of the m-completion
items.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of the usual Hecke algebra T. The strict algebra T' acts on H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_m. If for every good place w not above l the map H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_{m(w)} -> H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_m is an isomorphism, where m(w) is the induced maximal ideal of the prime-to-w Hecke algebra (true when Galois representations are attached to the cohomology: Khare-Thorne, Lemma 6.20), then the full T-tilde preserves H^*(Y(K), Z_l)_m.
items.locator: Section 2.14, (37), p. 27 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Criterion for the full T-tilde to preserve an m-completion. Used in Section 5.4 and before Proposition 8.6 ('by the argument of (37)'). Route: the Part II.

items.name: Reduction of coefficients is surjective at nice primes
items.statement: In the setting of Section 3.2, if l^n divides q_v - 1 and n > m, then the change-of-coefficients map H(G_v, K_v)_{Z/l^n} -> H(G_v, K_v)_{Z/l^m} is surjective. Via (41) this reduces to surjectivity of H^*(C, Z/l^n) -> H^*(C, Z/l^m) for a cyclic group C of order divisible by l^n.
items.locator: Section 3.4, p. 30 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Surjectivity of reduction of coefficients for local derived Hecke algebras, used in Section 2.13 to compare T-tilde with its finite-level pieces. Route: the SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups source route.

items.name: Derived Iwahori-Hecke algebra and derived bimodules
items.statement: With S = Z/l^r as in Section 4.1: H_I := Ext^*_{SG_v}(S[G_v/I_v], S[G_v/I_v]), H_IK := Ext^*_{SG_v}(S[G_v/K_v], S[G_v/I_v]) and H_KI := Ext^*_{SG_v}(S[G_v/I_v], S[G_v/K_v]), each with an invariant-function model as in Section 2.3 (classes in H^*(G_xy, S) on pairs of cosets). Yoneda composition gives H_KI (x) H_I (x) H_IK -> H_K = H(G_v, K_v) and H_KI (x) H_I^j (x) H_IK -> H_K^j, used in the proof of Theorem 7.6 and in (155).
items.locator: Section 4.6, p. 40; (155), p. 90 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The derived Iwahori-Hecke algebra and bimodules are the objects through which H^*(T_n) acts in the proof of Theorem 7.6 and through which Lemma 8.18 is proved. Only their restriction maps (item 31) are items. Route: the SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups source route.

items.name: Hecke-trivial cohomology is the cohomology of the compact dual
items.statement: In the setting of Section 5.1 (Y(K) compact), H^*(SU_d, C) = SL_d(C)-invariant forms on SL_d(C)/SU_d = H^*(Y(K), C)_triv (59). By a maximum-modulus argument, a harmonic form with T omega = deg(T) omega for one Hecke operator T is G(F (x) R)-invariant. Hence H^*(Y(K), C)_triv is a free exterior algebra on generators in degrees 3, 5, ..., 2d - 1, and for all large l, H^*(Y(K), Z/l)_triv is the free exterior algebra on the reductions of integral generators (Section 5.6 (iv)).
items.locator: Section 5.5, (59), pp. 45-46; Section 5.6 (iv), p. 46 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Computes the Hecke-trivial cohomology whose cyclicity is Theorem 5.2. It is a key input to Sections 5.4-5.8 and is not an item. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Hecke algebra acting on the chain complex
items.statement: T_{K_0} is the Z_p-algebra generated by the endomorphisms, in the derived category of Z_p-modules, of the Z_p-chain complex of Y(K_0) induced by the Hecke operators at good primes prime to p (following Khare-Thorne), so it acts on cohomology with coefficients in any Z_p-module. T_K at deeper level K is defined the same way with Hecke operators at good primes for K. Pi gives T_{K_0} -> Z_p (73); chi: T_{K_0} -> k and m = ker chi (74), and m is used at every level.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The Hecke algebra used in Sections 6-8 is defined in the derived sense (after Khare-Thorne), which differs from the item-3 algebra of endomorphisms of cohomology. The Taylor-Wiles argument uses this definition.

items.name: Local-global compatibility at auxiliary level and inertial level <= n
items.statement: (i) At Y_0(q): H_K, identified with the centre of H_I (Section 4.3), acts on H_*(Y_0(q), k)_m through the generalised eigencharacter by which it acts on Pi. (ii) Fix Frob^T in T^dual(k) conjugate to rho-bar(Frob_q). A deformation sigma of rho-bar ramified at q can be uniquely conjugated so that sigma restricted to G_{Q_q} factors through the profinite completion of Q_q^* -> T^dual(R), with a uniformiser reducing to Frob^T; restriction to F_q^* and duality give A(F_q) -> R^* (99). Local-global compatibility: the resulting action of A(F_q) on H^*(Y_1(q,n), Z_p)_{m,Frob^T}, through R^univ_{S u {q}} -> T_{K_1(q,n),m}, equals the deck-transformation action, in a derived-category and several-primes form (Galatius-Venkatesh, Section 13.5). (iii) A deformation has inertial level <= n at q if its restriction to F_q^* factors through F_q^*/p^n; R^{univ,<=n}_{S u {q}} is the quotient of R^univ_{S u {q}} by t - 1 for t in the image of p^n A(F_q) under (99) (100).
items.locator: Section 6.5, p. 61; Section 6.11, (99)-(100), pp. 67-68 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The local-global compatibility hypotheses at auxiliary level and the inertial-level condition. They define R_n (102) and the S_n-action (103), and they are used in Lemmas 6.6, 6.9 and 8.14. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Fontaine-Laffaille finite local condition and its duality
items.statement: Call a Gal(Q_p-bar/Q_p)-module on a finitely generated Z_p-module crystalline if it is a subquotient of a crystalline representation with Hodge weights in [-(p-3)/2, (p-3)/2]. For p-torsion crystalline M, H^1_f(Q_p, M) in H^1(Q_p, M) classifies the crystalline extensions. It is the cokernel of 1 - Frob: F^0 D(M) -> D(M), whose kernel is H^0(Q_p, M), so #H^1_f(Q_p, M) = |D(M)|/|F^0 D(M)| . #H^0(Q_p, M) (121). H^1_f(Q_p, M) and H^1_f(Q_p, M^*), with M^* = Hom(M, mu_{p^inf}), are exact annihilators under local duality.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The torsion Fontaine-Laffaille local condition and its self-duality underlie the definition of H^1_f(Z[1/S], -) and the proofs of Lemma 8.9 and (145)-(147). Item 47 only names the condition.

items.name: The map f_{q,n} to V/p^n
items.statement: For a Taylor-Wiles prime q of level n with chosen Frob^T_q, T_q = A(F_q)/p^n and alpha in H^1(T_q, Z/p^n), (139) gives alpha' in H^1(Q_q, Ad rho-bar_n)/H^1_ur(Q_q, Ad rho-bar_n). f_{q,n}(alpha) in V/p^n = Hom(H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)), Z/p^n) is beta -> <alpha', beta_q>_q, the local Tate pairing with the restriction of beta to Q_q (124). For a datum Q_n this gives f_{Q_n}: t_{S_n} = Hom(T_n, Z/p^n) ->> V/p^n (142).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): f_{q,n} is one of the two maps in the characterising property (*) of Theorem 8.5, but it is not defined in any item. Route: the Part II.

items.name: Cohomology is free over the exterior algebra on V
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Sections 6.1-6.2: W = t_S/t_R is isomorphic to V (168), compatibly with the actions, and H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m is a free Lambda^* V-module generated by H^q(Y(1), Z_p)_m. In particular V freely generates an exterior algebra inside End H^*(Y(1), Z_p)_m, contained in the strict global derived Hecke algebra.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): The strongest structural conclusion of Section 8: the cohomology is free over the exterior algebra on V. It sharpens Theorem 7.6 but is stated only inside the proof. Route: the Part II.

items.name: The classes [q, nu, alpha] and the map e_{psi,g}
items.statement: For a field k, psi in X^*(T^dual) and regular semisimple g in G^dual(k) with centraliser Z_g, e_{psi,g}: Lie(T^dual) -> Lie(Z_g) is the sum over the isomorphisms phi: T^dual -> Z_g (over k-bar) of <psi, phi^{-1}(g)> d(phi); it is defined over k, and for G^dual = SL_2 it sends diag(1,-1) to 2g - tr(g). For q unramified for rho with q = 1 mod p^n and rho-bar(Frob_q) strongly regular, nu strictly dominant (a character of T^dual) and alpha in H^1(A(F_q), Z/p^n) = Hom(F_q^*, X^*(T^dual)/p^n), push alpha, viewed in H^1(Q_q, Lie(T^dual)/p^n)/H^1_ur, forward along e_{nu,rho(Frob_q)}: Lie(T^dual) -> Ad rho (170), then pair with H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)) by local reciprocity. This defines [q, nu, alpha] in V/p^n.
items.locator: Section 8.28, (170), pp. 99-100 (Forum Math. Pi 7 (2019), e7)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (coverage of the published text): Lemma 8.29 (item 55) is stated in terms of [q, nu, alpha], which no item defines. Route: the Part II.
